addendum_hash_recipe.note: Recompute from this committed file alone; depends on every field except addendum_hash.

amendment_rule: Sealed before the effective day's first freeze; governs only forecasts frozen on or after it. Any further change is another dated addendum.
disclosure_of_timing: Written after the first outcomes existed. On the first 126 graded XRPL v2 rows (6 freeze days, 2026-09-23..28), the forecast was right on average (37.0% forecast vs 36.5% observed) while its Brier skill against hindsight climatology was -0.16. That early, overlapping sample decides nothing; it showed the gap. Because this rule only adds a test, scores only forecasts frozen after it is sealed, and cannot make any forecast look better, the timing cannot flatter any board.
not_covered: standing_acceptance_standard_mw_grid_v1 (a calibration probe of the same Market Weather forecasts whose MARKET stream is covered here; its groups are forecast-probability bins, for which a per-group climatology is not a meaningful baseline). SOL v2 (BBM tier family): its sealed standard already has EVIDENCE OF SKILL. The retired MC-forecast family (SOL v1 cohorts) keeps its sealed rule.

skill_rule.baseline: Per stratum, sample climatology: the stratum's own outcome rate over the same items, used as a constant forecast for every item in that stratum. This is the best constant forecast in hindsight, so it is harder to beat than any constant fixed in advance; a stratum where the outcome never happened has a perfect baseline and still counts the model's errors.
skill_rule.inference: Moving-block bootstrap over whole freeze days, blocks of the standard's block_days, the standard's resamples, seed = the standard's seed + seed_offset (99% interval: + seed_offset + 1). Climatology is re-estimated inside every resample.
skill_rule.items: Every RESOLVED item of the standard's own streams frozen on or after effective_from_freeze_day and inside the verdict's period. Near-certain forecasts are included: skill is scored on every forecast. VOID and INCOMPLETE rows are excluded exactly as the standard already excludes them.

results.NO SKILL SHOWN: >= shown_min_days matured freeze days since the effective day and neither of the above.
results.SKILL SHOWN: >= shown_min_days matured freeze days since the effective day, skill >= shown_min_skill and the shown_ci interval lies entirely above 0.
results.SKILL UNTESTED: Fewer than shown_min_days matured freeze days since the effective day (and not WORSE THAN CLIMATOLOGY), fewer than min_items items, or no stratum saw both outcomes.
results.WORSE THAN CLIMATOLOGY: >= worse_min_days matured freeze days since the effective day and the worse_ci interval of skill lies entirely below 0. Checked first.

skill_rule.statistic: skill = 1 - sum over strata of sum (p - y)^2 / sum over strata of n_g * ybar_g * (1 - ybar_g). Pooled over strata (summed, not averaged). 0 = no better than climatology; 1 = perfect.
skill_rule.strata: The standard's own groups: the band widths (and Market Weather's held positions), or the XRPL v2 / Fee Coverage events lose and lose1. Market Weather is judged per stream (MARKET, POOLS).

title: Breach-probability family addendum 3: skill is tested (a forecast that is right on average but tells pools apart no better than one number is not called useful)

what_changes.display: Wherever GradedLP shows a governed board's verdict, the SKILL result is shown next to it. CALIBRATED without SKILL SHOWN is described as right on average, not as useful for choosing between pools.
what_changes.new_result: Every verdict of a governed standard carries a 'skill' block per stream: the result (one of the four above), the deciding condition, pooled skill with its 95% and 99% intervals, and per-stratum n, outcome rate, Brier, climatology Brier and skill. Reported whether or not a result can fire yet.

what_does_not_change: Each standard's own verdict (INVALID / EVIDENCE AGAINST / CALIBRATED / UNTESTED), its conditions, thresholds, cadence and evaluation order; every forecast object, model, outcome rule, addendum 1 (confident calls) and addendum 2 (drained pools). The SKILL result never blocks, upgrades or downgrades a verdict. Items frozen before the effective day are never scored by this rule - it is not applied to any forecast or outcome that existed when it was sealed.
why: Every governed standard tests calibration only: whether outcomes happen about as often as forecast. Brier skill against climatology is reported but never gated, so a forecaster that gives every pool the same number can earn CALIBRATED while telling a user nothing about which pool is riskier. The question a user actually has - does this forecast tell pools apart better than a single number - had no sealed answer.
